PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION City Council recessed to Closed Session at 5:18 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council reconvened to Open Session at 6:38 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session items:

Items #4.B. and #4.C. were not discussed in the Closed Session.  

Items #1, #3 and item #4.A - Staff made a presentation, direction was provided and no reportable action was taken on any of these items.   

Item #2- only one matter was discussed.  Staff made a presentation, direction was provided and no reportable action was taken on these items.  

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called regular meeting to order at 6:38 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT Gloria Nezahualcoya voiced her concerns regarding the Director of Transportation's ongoing use of a City car since 2018. She expressed dissatisfaction with the response to her Public Records Request, stating that the provided documentation did not sufficiently justify the Director's need for the vehicle.




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Ivan Altamirano Councilmember Garcia requested that items #6 and #8 be pulled for discussion.

Item #6 - Councilmember Garcia asked for additional information regarding previous amendments. Director of Transportation McFerguson explained that Amendment #2 included environmental components that needed to be completed, and Amendment #3 modified and expanded the scope of the project, including driveway repavement, design modifications, and ADA compliance. Councilmember Garcia requested that the staff and architect collaborate to finalize these details and avoid the need for further amendments.

Director of Transportation McFerguson acknowledged that due to the project's size, some changes may be unforeseen, but the staff will make efforts to minimize the need for additional amendments. City Manager Cisneros recommended approving Amendment #4, which amounts to $44,000 and has a specific scope identified in the staff report. Councilmember Rebollo mentioned that the funding for the project comes from federal funds. The Director of Transportation added that soil testing is required before the demolition begins.

Councilmember Rebollo made a motion to approve the Fourth Amendment to the Professional Service Agreement between the City of Commerce and Stantec Architecture Incorporated for architecture and engineering services, with Vice Mayor Altamirano seconding the motion. The motion was carried with the following vote:

AYES: Councilmembers Garcia, Lainez, Rebollo, Vice Mayor Altamirano, and Mayor Argumedo (5)

Item #8 - Councilmember Garcia inquired about how candidates are retained after completing training, specifically regarding the specifications. Greg explained that team-building and flexible schedules are implemented to allow candidates to pursue other endeavors. In response to Councilmember Garcia, Director Alaniz clarified that lifeguards and instructor guards would be compensated during their training. Further discussion arose about acceptable IDin order to qualify for the positions.  City Manager Cisneros stated that anyone lawfully allowed to work in the United States would qualify.

Councilmember Rebollo expressed support for the idea of hiring alumni during the summer and providing them with flexibility when they attend college. 

Councilmember Rebollo made a motion to adopt a Resolution amending the Classification and Compensation Plan by revising the job specifications for the Lifeguard and Instructor Guard classification. Councilmember Garcia seconded the motion. The motion was carried with the following vote:

AYES: Councilmembers Garcia, Lainez, Rebollo, Vice Mayor Altamirano, and Mayor Argumedo (5)
